risk_note: RV2 orders read paths (FU-ORDERS-OWN-LOOKUP-INDEX; rulings D10-851 ①, D10-853). Lookups of app.orders by order number no longer scan an app's orders: exact sub-order lookups (taobao / jd) resolve (order_id, attr_at) through app.order_keys and read orders by primary key (admin order search, H5 claim, rights lookup, snapshot retry read and due scan); parent-order lookups use orders_parent_order_idx (B1-09w); the admin search and readOwnTaobaoOrderNos split their sub OR parent into two branches of one UNION ALL (count and page from the same source, no duplicates). readOwnTaobaoOrderNos drives the sub branch from order_keys with a LATERAL primary-key read and the parent branch with unnest + LATERAL per value ending in a literal OFFSET 0: real EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on the test database without statistics showed that a multi-value parent IN, and an un-fenced LATERAL that PostgreSQL pulls up, both fall back to an app_id-only index scan (1200 / 600 rows per partition); with OFFSET 0 each value is a parameterised index lookup (21 buffers). Results are unchanged; pdd hyphen-stripped matching and the H5 order search are untouched (FU-PDD-ORDERNO-NORMALIZED-INDEX). Frozen [AC-B1-09c#20-22] (one statement, no OR) and taobao-refund-archive expectOwnOrderRead still hold. Integration own-lookup-index plus the related frozen order / union directories 304/304 pass (re-run after the round-3 kit move); rule-test unit 93/93.

reviews.note: codex-run.sh review --review-type money (D10-823): round 1 over the whole implementation diff from the last rule-test commit (rounds 1-2 of the implementation) pass with no findings; round 2 over the increment (implementation rounds 3-4: the parent branch's unnest + LATERAL and OFFSET 0) pass with no findings; checklist rounding na, sign na, idempotency ok, concurrency ok, partial_refund na, clock na/ok, app_id ok. The integration run was the gate between rounds; the plan behaviour was confirmed by EXPLAIN, not by Codex (static review).
